These Miscellaneous First Appeals coming on for admission this day, the court delivered the following:
 JUDGMENT MFA No. 9077/2017 is filed by the National Insurance Company Limited ('insurance company' for brevity) challenging the negligence attributed entirely on the driver of the motor cycle and also challenging the quantum of compensation.
MFA No. 7953/2017 is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. Brief facts:
The claimants are the husband and children of one Sannamma.

On 23.03.2016 at about 5.30 p.m., the said Sannamma was moving on a motor cycle bearing registration No. KA-16-EA-3437 as pillion rider from Kallahatti to Bharamasagara Village after completion of her daily coolie work.

At that time the rider of the aforesaid motor cycle ridden the motor cycle in rash and negligent manner without following the traffic rules and toppled down and due to the said incident, Sannamma sustained multiple injuries on her head and vital parts of the body.
Immediately she was shifted to Government Hospital, Chitradurga and from there to higher hospitals.
On 25.3.2016 she died.
3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the claimants under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation.
The deceased was doing coolie work and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
The claimants who are the husband and children were depending upon the earning of the deceased.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the petition in part, and awarded a compensation of Rs.9,03,600/-, along with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
The Tribunal held the rider of the motor cycle was negligent in riding the bus.

4. The Tribunal has awarded compensation to the claimants as under : -
1 Loss of dependency Rs. 6,33,600/-

2 Loss of estate Rs.20,000/-
3 Loss of love and affection Rs.1,00,000/- 4 Loss of consortium Rs.50,000/-
5. Mental shock and agony Rs.50,000/-
6. Funeral expenses Rs.50,000/-

sentences.text: The learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that the deceased had self fallen on the ground and therefore negligence is not on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.
Hence, insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
Further submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
Therefore prays for reducing the same.

6. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the claimants submitted that the rider of the motor cycle was negligent and hence the Tribunal has correctly fastened the liability on the insurance company.
Further submitted the quantum of compensation awarded is on the lesser side and therefore prays for enhancement of the same.
7. The IMV report, charge sheet and MLC extract produced in the case show that while the deceased was riding as a pillion rider on the motor cycle, had fallen from the same.
Ex.P29-Nimhans case sheet stated that the deceased had felt giddiness while traveling as a pillion rider on the motor cycle and fallen from the bike.
Therefore it is proved that the deceased while traveling as a pillion rider on the motor bike had fallen from the bike and sustained fatal injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
Just because the deceased was feeling giddiness while riding as a pillion rider, it does not mean that the rider of the motor cycle was not rash and negligent in driving the motor cycle.
The deceased is a woman.
The entire complaint is against the rider of the motor cycle in riding the bike in a rash and negligent manner.
Charge sheet is also filed against the rider of the motor cycle.
Therefore, the deceased had fallen from the bike and succumbed to the injuries.
Hence, the Tribunal is correct in holding that the rider of the motor cycle was completely negligent.
Also to meet the contention raised by the insurance company that the motor bike was implicated, but there is no evidence to prove that the motor cycle was implicated.
Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in holding that the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No. KA-16-EA-3437 has caused the accident.
It is proved that the deceased while traveling as a pillion rider had fallen from the motor bike due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motor bike.
Therefore, the contention taken by the learned counsel for the insurance company is not accepted.
8. The claimants are husband and four children.
Deceased was working as a coolie and a home maker.
The deceased died in the accident while she was returning to the house after completion of her coolie work.

The Tribunal has committed an error in taking the notional income as Rs.6,000/-
per month.
Considering the date of accident, 23.3.2016, notional income of Rs.9,500/- per month is to be taken into consideration.

The deceased was 45 years on the date of accident, therefore 25%
income (Rs.2,375/-)is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.
There are five dependents.
1/4th amount is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
But, the Tribunal has committed an error in taking 1/5th.
Hence it is modified.
Appropriate multiplier is '14'.

Therefore, loss of dependency is reassessed as follows:
Rs.9,500 + 2,375/- (25% of Rs.9,500/) x 3/4 x 14 x 12 = Rs.14,96,250/-.

sentences.text: Further the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding compensation under other heads and they have to be modified.
There are five dependents.
Hence, each claimants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- under the head 'loss of consortium' as per the decision in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others [2018 ACJ 2782].

sentences.text: 10% is to be added towards - 10 - escalation.

Therefore, Rs.2,20,000/- is awarded to the claimants under the head 'loss of consortium'.
10.
Further compensation of Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards 'transportation and obsequies ceremony' and Rs.16,500/- towards 'loss of estate'.
11. The claimants have produced medical bills amounting to Rs.21,625/-.
As the claimants have spent the said amount to save the life of the deceased, Rs.21,625/- is awarded towards medical expenses.

12. Thus, in all the claimants are entitled to compensation as under : -
1 Loss of dependency Rs. 14,96,250/- 2 Loss of consortium Rs.2,20,000/-

3 Funeral and obsequies ceremony Rs.16,500/- 4 Loss of estate Rs.16,500/-
5.
Medical expenses Rs.21,625/-
. The Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 9% p.a.

The same is scaled down to 6% p.a.
14.
The claimants are entitled for a total enhanced compensation of Rs.17,70,875/- as against Rs.9,03,600/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, the claimants are entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.8,67,275/- (Rs.17,70,875/- - Rs.9,03,600/-), along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
15. Accordingly, I pass the following ORDER i.
Both the appeals are allowed in part.
